short: One of the Italian pioneers of electroconvulsive therapy.
note: Ugo Cerletti and Lucio Bini, Italian physicians who introduced electroconvulsive therapy in Rome in April 1938. Bini designed the original electrical apparatus.

short: An old term for a psychiatrist.
note: A physician who specializes in mental disorders; an older term for a psychiatrist.
German Blutsauger means a bloodsucker, literally or figuratively, and can mean a vampire.
Sigmund Freud (1856–1939), the Austrian physician who developed psychoanalysis, emphasizing unconscious mental processes and the interpretation of dreams.

short: Approaching a limit without reaching it.
note: In a way that continually approaches a limiting value, becoming arbitrarily close without attaining that value.

short: The scientist in the Buck Rogers comic strip.
note: Doctor Huer is Buck Rogers’s scientist friend in the newspaper science-fiction adventure strip that began in 1929.

short: A fashionably unconventional young woman of the 1920s.
note: A young woman associated especially with the 1920s who challenged conventional expectations through her dress and behavior.

short: A brand of machines for recording spoken dictation.
note: A brand of office recording machines used to capture speech for later transcription. Early Dictaphones recorded on wax cylinders.
